description: Mainly an endgame unit. Fires when column 4 is full, the right side is full or nearly full (column 5 full, or columns 5+6 together hold 10 or more stones), and columns 1 and 2 still have room. Strongest when the side to move is losing. A weaker early-game part: the opponent has a vertical three in column 4 or 5 that must be blocked on top. Full columns 4 and 5 alone are not enough.
effect: Small. Forcing it high nudges the move toward column 1 (about +0.02 to +0.07) and away from column 2 (about -0.05). No measurable change in forced-move positions.
notes: 8 score calls. Threat or evaluation proxies (poisoned columns, parity threats, column control) scored badly (F1 0.10-0.20). Column-height rules did much better. Best was p8 (heights plus a col 4/5 vertical-three must-block clause): F1 0.493 (P 0.441, R 0.559), AUROC 0.769, simulation share 0.15. Activation depends a lot on context: one stone can move it from -0.4 to 4.3 with the same coarse heights, which fits it tracking the engine's 'side to move is lost' late in the game (band 9 is 14/15 lost). It is higher at odd ply in several games. Synthesis: one sequence reached 9.685, above the dev max of 9.405.
